names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 22 decembrie, «Sfântul Mucenic Hrisogon», with the rank words left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 24 Νοεμβρίου, «Άγιος Χρυσόγονος», with the rank word left off.

The nominative behind days.pravoslavie.ru's line for 22 декабря ст. ст., which declines it to «Хрисогона»; the calendar's life of the company spells it «Хрисогон». His name page gives no epithet with it.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 22 декабря ст. ст. — «Мчч. Хрисогона, Феодотии, Евода, Евтихиана и иных (ок. 304).»

attestations.note: He heads the company on this calendar's line, and his name page 2351 keeps him on this one day. saint.gr keeps him on 24 Νοεμβρίου instead, and that is a different day and not a style conversion of this one.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 22 decembrie — «Sfântul Mucenic Hrisogon»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Νοεμβρίου — «Άγιος Χρυσόγονος»

attestations.note: The life page `https://www.saint.gr/2989/saint.aspx` heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 24 Νοεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», and the man is the folder's own: a Christian of Rome of noble birth and higher education, imprisoned under Diocletian, who sustained many of the faithful from his prison and was killed and thrown into the sea. **The folder's Romanian row keeps him on 22 December and this Greek row keeps him on 24 November, and that is one row per church and not a second commemoration invented.** The Greek page tells the part the Romanian life does not: the offer of honours, the axe, and the priest Zoilos who found the body in the sea and buried it secretly in his own house. It does not name Anastasia, whom the Romanian life makes his pupil; the two accounts agree in the city, the rank, the imprisonment under Diocletian and the sea. **No `dates` object is proposed**, because the page names Diocletian and prints no year at all. No hymn. No asterisk and not the sentence «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη η ύπαρξη του Αγίου».
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (28 September 2026).
